title: OpenAVC Driver Definition (.avcdriver)
description: The schema for OpenAVC .avcdriver device driver definitions. Use it for live validation and autocompletion in your editor while authoring drivers. The required fields and constraints match what the OpenAVC community driver catalog enforces. Loaded on its own, the OpenAVC platform requires only id, name, and transport; the remaining metadata fields (manufacturer, category, version, author, description, source_url) are required to publish a driver to the community catalog.

id.description: Unique driver identifier. Lowercase alphanumeric with underscores.

manufacturer.description: Manufacturer name. Must exist in manufacturers.json for catalog submission.

category.description: Driver category. One of the ten catalog categories.

transport.description: Transport the driver uses to reach the device.

transports.description: Optional. Transports this driver can use interchangeably (e.g. ["tcp", "serial"] for a text protocol whose command/response strings are byte-identical over the network or a serial line). The per-device connection picks the actual transport; listing "serial" makes the device offerable over a direct serial port or through a bridge. Opt-in: only declare it when the strings really are identical across the listed media.

bridge.description: Optional. Declares this driver as a bridge: a device that exposes typed ports other devices connect through (e.g. a serial-to-Ethernet adapter). The port declaration is valid in YAML; pushing serial line settings to the hardware (the prepare_bridge_port hook) needs a Python driver.

ports.description: The typed ports this bridge advertises.

id.description: Port id referenced by a downstream device's bridge_port (e.g. "serial:1").

kind.description: Port kind. A serial port vends a transparent TCP pass-through; ir/relay ports route commands through the bridge at send time.

passthrough_port.description: For serial ports: the TCP port on the bridge host that transparently pipes this serial line (e.g. 4999).

label.description: Human-readable port label shown in the connection picker.

description.description: Brief description of what the driver controls.

source_url.description: Protocol reference or product documentation URL. Must start with http:// or https://.

delimiter.description: Message delimiter. Default "\r". Use "\r\n" for CRLF. Escape sequences \r and \n are interpreted.

inline_protocol.description: Built-in generic devices only. When true, the device page shows a no-code Commands & Responses editor that stores commands/responses/state_variables in the device config and merges them into this driver at runtime. Community drivers ship their commands and responses in the driver file and should not set this.

ports.description: TCP/UDP ports the device listens on (catalog metadata only).

protocols.description: Protocol names this driver speaks, e.g. ["pjlink"]. Helps discovery match devices to drivers.

simulated.description: True if the driver ships with simulator support (auto-gen or an explicit simulator: section).

verified.description: True once the driver has been validated against real hardware.

min_platform_version.description: Minimum OpenAVC version required. Blocks install on older platforms missing a needed feature. Semantic version.

deprecated.description: True if this driver is superseded. Requires replacement_id.

replacement_id.description: ID of the driver that replaces this one. Only valid when deprecated is true.

compatible_models.description: Specific device models this driver supports, with confidence levels.

default_config.description: Default values for config fields (e.g. host, port, poll_interval, inter_command_delay).

config_derived.description: Computed config values, each a template substituted from other config fields, e.g. {"ws": "/workspace/{workspace_id}"}. If any {field} the template references is empty or missing, the derived value is "" — so an optional prefixed address segment simply disappears. Computed once when the device connects and visible to every command address, on_connect entry, response, and poll query (just like a real config field). Lets one friendly field (e.g. a workspace id) drive both a bare and a prefixed address form without conditional logic in every command.

config_schema.description: Per-device connection settings shown in the Add Device dialog. Keyed by config field name.

device_settings.description: Configurable values that live on the device hardware (polled + writable). Keyed by setting name.

state_variables.description: Read-only state properties this driver exposes. Keyed by state variable name.

propertyNames.description: Child type names become state-key segments (device.<id>.<child_type>...) and feed fnmatch dispatch, so they must not contain dots or glob metacharacters (. * ? [).

child_entity_types.description: Sub-units this device manages (encoders, decoders, zones, presets). Keyed by child type name.

commands.description: Commands this driver can send. Keyed by command name.

quick_actions.description: Command ids promoted to one-click Quick Action buttons at the top of the device view. Sugar for actions of kind "command". Each id must name a declared command.

actions.description: Driver-declared actions promoted to buttons in the device view. kind:"command" promotes a declared command (runs online); kind:"setup" is an offline-capable provisioning wizard handled by the driver's run_setup_action().

responses.description: Patterns for parsing device replies. Regex/OSC rules are checked in order and the first match wins; a json: true rule parses the whole JSON body and applies all of its field mappings, so a multi-field JSON reply fully populates.

on_connect.description: Commands sent immediately after connect, before polling. Strings for TCP/serial/UDP; {address, args} mappings for OSC.

queries.description: Query strings (or command names) sent each poll cycle. Cadence comes from default_config.poll_interval.

polling.description: Periodic status query configuration. NOTE: a polling.interval key is inert and rejected by the catalog validator; set the cadence via default_config.poll_interval instead.

connection.description: Optional short troubleshooting hint shown on the device's offline banner when it can't connect (e.g. a remote-access setting that must be enabled on the device first).

helpBlock.description: Help text shown in the Add Device dialog and available to the AI assistant. overview + setup are required; connection is optional.

label.description: Human-readable label. Required for top-level state variables.

childStateVariableEntry.description: Child state variable. Same shape as device state variables, but label is not required (the platform injects online and label automatically).

type.description: Only integer local IDs are supported in v1.

child_type.description: For child_id type: the child_entity_types name this parameter targets.

options_state.description: Make this param a picker sourced from a device-relative state key. The IDE reads device.<id>.<options_state> (a JSON-encoded list of strings or {value,label} objects) and offers it as a dropdown. The driver publishes the enumerable set as a state variable.

options_source.description: Like options_state but an absolute state key, read verbatim (same primitive plugins use). Use options_state for per-device lists.

options_from.description: Cascade: source this param's options from a sibling param's chosen value.

param.description: The sibling param whose value selects the option set.

source.description: child_schema: offer the controls of the child picked in the sibling child_id param.

type_from.description: Make this param's input type follow the control chosen in a sibling cascade. The named param is itself an options_from child_schema cascade; this param then renders as that control's type (number+range, Yes/No, etc.).

param.description: The sibling options_from(child_schema) param whose chosen control supplies this param's type/min/max.

type.description: OSC type tag: f=float32, i=int32, s=string, h=int64, d=float64, T=true, F=false, N=nil.

send.description: Raw bytes to send (TCP/serial/UDP). {param} and {config} placeholders substituted at runtime.

body.description: HTTP request body. Parsed as JSON when valid, otherwise sent raw.

commandEntry.description: A command must declare one of: send (TCP/serial/UDP), path/method (HTTP), or address (OSC).

id.description: Unique action id within the driver.

kind.description: Promotes a declared command (runs online via send_command). Default and only value for .avcdriver drivers. Offline-capable 'setup' provisioning wizards require a Python driver with a run_setup_action() handler.

label.description: Button label. Defaults to the promoted command's label, else the id.

icon.description: lucide icon name (kebab-case), e.g. power, shield, search, radar.

confirm.description: Confirm before running. true for a generic prompt, or a custom message string.

availability.description: When the button shows. online (default) hides while offline; offline shows only while offline; always ignores connection state.

command.description: kind:"command" only — the command id to send. Defaults to the action id.

params.description: Input dialog fields. For kind:"command", defaults to the promoted command's params.

actionEntry.description: A promoted action. kind:"command" must resolve to a declared command (the command field, or the id).

visibleWhen.description: Show the action only when a state condition holds. A single {key, operator, value} condition, or an {any:[...]} (OR) / {all:[...]} (AND) group. key may use $id for the device's own id.

key.description: State key compared against. May contain $id (replaced with the device id).

value.description: Value to compare against (not needed for truthy/falsy).

group.description: Regex capture group index (1-based; 0 is the whole match).

type.description: Coercion applied to the captured value.

map.description: Lookup table translating raw captured values to friendly values.

json_path.description: Optional. The matched value is treated as a JSON string: it is parsed and this dot-separated path is walked (object keys and integer list indices, e.g. "data" or "data.name" or "data.0") to the value used before mapping/coercion. A path landing on an array or object yields its length (so a boolean type becomes "is non-empty?" and an integer type becomes the count). Omit for today's positional/raw behavior. Common for OSC devices whose replies carry the value inside a JSON string (e.g. QLab's /reply ... {"data": ...}).

json.description: When true, the whole reply body is parsed as a JSON object and every set/mappings key is read from it. Unlike regex responses, all json rules are applied to a body (not just the first match), so one JSON reply can populate many state variables. In this mode a set value is the JSON field to read (a string key, dot path allowed) or a {key, type, map} object, not a capture ref.

match.description: Regex matched against incoming text. Capture groups extract values.

address.description: OSC address pattern (must start with /). Supports fnmatch wildcards.

set.description: Shorthand mapping state variables to values. For regex responses, values are capture groups ("$1") or static values. For a json: true response, values are JSON field names (dot path allowed) or {key, type, map} specs.

mappings.description: Verbose mapping form, supporting type coercion and value maps.

responseEntry.description: A response must declare match or pattern (regex), address (OSC), or json: true (JSON-body).

authBlock.description: Telnet-style login handshake. Only valid on tcp/serial transports (it reads a raw byte stream); declaring it on udp/http/osc is rejected at load time. username_prompt and password_prompt are required. All four regexes are checked for catastrophic backtracking since they run on raw pre-auth device bytes.

type.description: Handshake type. Only telnet_login is implemented and accepted.

username_prompt.description: Regex matched against the device's username prompt. Required.

password_prompt.description: Regex matched against the device's password prompt. Required.

username_field.description: Config field holding the username. Default "username".

password_field.description: Config field holding the password. Default "password".

skip_if_empty.description: Skip the handshake when the username config is empty. Default true.

line_ending.description: Line ending appended to credentials. Default "\r\n".

type.description: Frame parser kind interpreted at runtime.

header_size.description: length_prefix: big-endian bytes holding the body length. Must be 1, 2, or 4. Default 2.

header_offset.description: length_prefix: added to the length the header decodes to. Use a negative value (e.g. -header_size) when the length field counts the header bytes themselves, so only the body is read. Default 0.

include_header.description: length_prefix: whether the parsed frame includes the header bytes (true) or just the body (false). Default false.

length.description: fixed_length: frame size in bytes. Default 1.

secret.description: Render as a masked password field.

state_key.description: State variable providing the current value. Defaults to the setting key.

setup.description: Prompt for this setting when adding the device to a project. Default false.

unique.description: Generate a non-clashing default (appends device ID). Default false.

deviceSettingEntry.description: type, label, help, and default are expected by the IDE; the runtime enforces only the write definition.

send.description: TCP/serial write string. {value} and config placeholders substituted.

push_state.description: Push state changes to connected drivers, matching real device feedback behavior.

error_modes.description: Named error behaviors selectable in the simulator UI.

controls.description: Declarative control widgets for the simulator UI.

receive.description: Regex pattern matched against incoming commands (template handler).

match.description: Regex pattern matched against incoming commands (template or script handler).

address.description: OSC address fnmatch pattern (OSC script handler).

notifications.description: Unsolicited messages emitted on state change, keyed by state variable.

oui.description: MAC OUI prefixes (vendor) used as a soft hint.

hostname.description: Hostname regex patterns used as a soft hint.

port_open.description: Open-port hints. Generic admin/web/SSH ports are disallowed.

manufacturer_alias.description: Vendor-string aliases matched against discovered banners/TXT records.

discoveryBlock.description: Discovery fingerprints and hints. Unknown keys are rejected by the platform and the catalog validator.

tls.description: Wrap the connection in TLS (no cert verification) before send/read, for an HTTPS-only device. Default false. tcp_probe only.

tcpProbe.description: TCP probe. Connect-only probes may omit send and expect. If it sends bytes, exactly one matcher is required.

udpProbe.description: UDP probe. Must declare a send payload (send_hex or send_ascii) and exactly one matcher.

pythonProbe.description: Python discovery escape-hatch. Bare path string or {file, cross_vendor} mapping. The companion .py must ship alongside the driver.
